newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Mine blast in Burundi kills 12 - defence ministry.
newsitem.headline: Mine blast in Burundi kills 12 - defence ministry.

text.p: Twelve civilians were killed when a minibus hit and detonated an anti-tank mine on a road south of Burundi's capital Bujumbura, the Defence Ministry said on Monday.
"A minibus rolled over an anti-tank mine on National Route 3...the mine was laid by rebels," a ministry official told Reuters.
The bus was carrying 18 passengers through Muhuta Commune, 30 km (18 miles) south of Bujumbura. Twelve people were killed and five were wounded by the mine explosion, the official said.
On August 4, four civilians were killed when a minibus detonated a mine on the same road.
On the same day another nine people were killed and nine were wounded when their bus set off a mine on its way to the capital from northwestern Cibitoke province, state-run radio said.

In the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa, the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) said on Monday it had appointed Ambassador Mamadou Bah of Guinea as its special representative to Burundi, taking over from Leardne Bassole of Burkina Faso.
More than 150,000 people have died in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since the assassination of Burundi's first Hutu president in October 1993.
